<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `dirhop.install` script contains standard AUR post-install and post-upgrade hooks that display a helpful message to the user via a shell heredoc. The function `_dirhop_note` outputs instructions on how to set up the `dho` command, suggesting the user either run it once or execute `dho --setup`. This is typical behavior for shell integration tools and falls within expected packaging practices.

The `post_install` function simply calls this note, which is common for packages that require user action to complete setup. The `post_upgrade` function conditionally shows the note only when upgrading from a version earlier than 0.2.1-1, using `vercmp` to compare versions—a standard and safe practice in AUR install scripts.

There are no network operations, file modifications outside expected scope, dangerous command executions, or obfuscated payloads. The script does not exfiltrate data, download remote content, or alter system behavior beyond printing a setup reminder. All operations are transparent and aligned with the package's stated purpose.
</details>
